issues.title: 01 — Mission State and Record Loading

source_acceptance.text: The user can run a local command and see the current Product Requirements Document title, Issue Slice count, blockers, and readiness summary.
Issue Slices are loaded from local markdown tracker records and ordered by dependency.
App-local runtime state is persisted outside the target repo and keyed by project identity.
The target repo is not polluted with bulky runtime state.
Missing or malformed issue records produce actionable errors instead of crashes.

issues.gap: Tracker/PRD loading and authoritative dependency order are absent; task namespaces cover only isolated local task state. Accepted local task candidates now compose into verified isolated child baselines with conflict refusal and durable input provenance; native tracker graph parity and workspace branch publication remain incomplete.

issues.title: 02 — Review Locking and Assignment

source_acceptance.text: The user can approve, hold, or request revision for an Issue Slice from the local command surface.
Approval locks slice goal, acceptance criteria, blockers, HITL/AFK classification, risk level, and evidence requirements.
Assigned model agent, launch order, and optional Local Agent notes remain editable before launch.
Attempts to change locked fields after approval are rejected unless the user explicitly unlocks the slice.
The review state is persisted and visible in the mission board summary.

issues.gap: Approval/reset guards exist; slice contract locking, explicit reopen and assignment-note continuity are absent.

issues.title: 03 — Launch Local Agent Session

source_acceptance.text: Only approved Issue Slices with satisfied blockers can launch.
Launch creates a mission-scoped Local Agent session record tied to one primary Issue Slice.
The task packet contains the slice goal, acceptance criteria, allowed paths, command policy, evidence requirements, and assignment.
The isolated worktree path is outside the target repo.
Accepted or completed worktrees are marked cleanup-eligible rather than deleted.

issues.gap: Explicit dispatch starts ready Approved tasks only after Accepted dependencies, with common worker/receipt guards and per-approval retry suppression. Native Issue Slice/session/task-packet parity, configured roles and governed cleanup eligibility remain incomplete.

issues.title: 04 — Command and Visibility Policy

source_acceptance.text: Commands are classified before execution and blocked or marked approval-required when policy demands it.
Project-specific command approvals can be recorded in app-local runtime state.
File visibility classification is available to task packet and review generation.
Local-only files cause Frontier Reviewer limitations to be explicit.
Blocked files are excluded from Frontier Model context.

issues.gap: Exact file/check sandbox policy exists; classified command approvals, visibility tiers and contextual expiring path grants are absent.

issues.title: 05 — Evidence Package Validation

source_acceptance.text: Evidence Packages can be recorded for a Local Agent session.
Missing required evidence blocks review with clear validation errors.
Evidence links are stored without embedding bulky raw evidence in mission Markdown.
Known risks and proposed context updates are visible in the review summary.
Evidence validation result is persisted in mission state.

issues.gap: Digest-bound diff/check evidence exists; full required-evidence schema, risks and proposed context updates are absent.

issues.title: 06 — Frontier Review and Repair Policy

source_acceptance.text: Review outcomes support Approved, Approved with limitations, Needs repair, Needs human review, and Rejected.
Missing or invalid evidence prevents Approved outcomes.
First rejection routes repair to the same Local Agent.
Second rejection routes repair to a fresh Local Agent.
Repeated architecture failure routes back to Frontier Architect revision.
Critical, security, or merge-risk failure escalates to the user.

issues.gap: Readable check/diff/output review and exact inspected-task shorthand validate evidence; explicit receipt-linked repair inherits policy with fresh approval and verified prior context. Automatic repair routing, limited approval, architect escalation and integrated timeline remain absent. Accepted results now support verified local review-branch handoff; remote publication and active-branch merge remain separate.

Runtime state and bulky evidence remain outside the target repo.

A returning agent can identify the next action by reading the mission summary first.

issues.gap: Native Linux archive, installed-binary PTY acceptance and noninteractive storage/model/Git/tool diagnostics exist; OS/glibc matrix, public entrypoint, license review and desktop npm compatibility decision remain unverified.

issues.title: 21 — Add Headless Alfredo Cli Grammar

source_acceptance.text: `alfredo run --agent <agent-id> "<prompt>"` executes terminal-only model work and returns clear lifecycle output suitable for automation.
`alfredo review --agent <agent-id>` and `alfredo review <session-id> --agent <agent-id>` run review-oriented work without launching the desktop UI.
`alfredo agents` lists configured agents and models using the provider-neutral model registry vocabulary.
Per-command `--agent` is the canonical scripting grammar for headless commands, and invalid agent ids fail with actionable guidance.
Terminal-only work still respects Orchestrator governance, command policy, path grants, model assignment, and Evidence Package boundaries.

issues.gap: Rust has interactive CLI flags only; headless run/review/agents grammar is absent.

issues.title: 22 — Build the Prompt Dominant Workstation Shell

source_acceptance.text: The desktop workstation opens to a two-zone layout with the prompt pane as the dominant working surface and Agent Workstations as a persistent side pane.

The active prompt composer remains pinned at the bottom while prior turns scroll independently.

Constrained-width behavior keeps the prompt, composer, critical status, and side-pane decisions reachable without overlapping content.

issues.gap: Terminal layout/composer exists; complete scope/status boundary and simultaneous task/conversation layout equivalence remain incomplete.

issues.title: 23 — Project Live Agent Workstation Cards

source_acceptance.text: Each live card shows agent or subagent name, actual model, role, current task, status, phase or progress, last activity, approval blockers, files touched count, latest command or test summary, and next action.
Card status covers thinking, running, waiting approval, blocked, reviewing, review-ready, done, and failed states from canonical Orchestrator/session state.

Blocked and waiting-approval cards sort above other live work, active work is grouped separately from done or historical sessions, and optional mission or scope grouping is available when many sessions exist.
The UI may show pending intent immediately, but accepted state appears only after Orchestrator acknowledgement with the expected revision.
Projection tests prove cards update from canonical state and do not derive accepted state from frontend-only assumptions.

issues.gap: Selected task status/progress/evidence and bounded live check stdout/stderr exist; nested delegation tree, attention priority, role, activity trail and selected-only tool-output subscription are absent.

issues.title: 24 — Expand Workstation Cards for Operational Detail

source_acceptance.text: Expanded cards show tool activity, files touched, diffs, Evidence Package links, relevant terminal excerpts, review state, and available governed actions for the selected agent or subagent.

issues.gap: Selected-task evidence is inspectable; live tool excerpts, pin/filter/sort and durable full activity are incomplete.

issues.title: 26 — Cover the Governed Workstation Action Family

source_acceptance.text: Launch, retry, cancel, approval, rejection, deferral, and path grant decisions cannot bypass Orchestrator validation or expected-revision checks.

issues.gap: Typed revision/correlation task actions exist; natural-language receipt-bound action routing, all action classes, actor/reason attribution and journal are incomplete.
